role.altitude: The industrial designer keeps observing users, judging needs, visiting shows, generating concepts and agreeing the line's look with others; first sweeps of reviews and publications, tagging references, merging comments and rewriting spec sheets shrink a little.
skills_to_grow: Checking every source and quote a research tool returns before using it
role.ambitious_version: A designer who reads every customer review of the range, not a sample, before planning the next product.

tasks.short: Gather market data and customer reviews, observe and interview users, judge the potential need for new products, and participate in new product planning.

steps.what: Industrial designer gathers market data, customer reviews and competitor ranges

loop.input: Customer reviews and return reasons for the range and competing products.
loop.output: Themes of praise and complaint, each with quoted reviews and counts.
loop.check: Each theme must quote reviews that exist in the source. The designer reads the quotes under each theme and checks the theme says what they say and that its count is plausible; unclear themes are read in full.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reviews describe the same problem in many different words.

steps.what: Industrial designer observes and interviews users
Industrial designer studies the potential need for new products and judges the opportunities
Industrial designer participates in new product planning meetings and documents

tasks.design: A summarising step groups customer reviews and return reasons for the range and competitors into themes with quoted reviews and counts, so the designer reads themes and samples instead of scrolling through reviews. Sales and competitor data come from the existing reports. Observing users, judging the need and planning stay with the designer and team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Only a sample of reviews could be read by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Models that group text into themes with quotes.
tasks.still_hard: Needs users cannot put into words.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the problem a user works around without noticing.

ambition.what: Read all reviews of the range each planning round instead of a sample.

tasks.altitude: Faster desk research; insight stays human.

evidence.claim: Research tasks suit an answer desk citing the pages it read, with a designer opening every link.

assumptions: Boundary: research for product planning; designing the product is outside.
Input contract for s1: reviews and return reasons exported from the webshop and retailer portals by the e-commerce team; competitor reviews from public pages.
User research, judgement and planning meetings keep their full time; only reading reviews changes.
research_questions: Do review themes predict which features sell?

already_counted.description: Industrial designer reads sampled reviews under each theme.

incremental.description: Industrial designer asks the e-commerce team for fresh review exports each round.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: products with few reviews, so themes add little (s1 90) (2.3); high: consumer products with many reviews (7.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read publications, attend showings, study competing products and design styles and motifs, file references and generate design concepts.

steps.what: Industrial designer reads publications and online sources on design styles and motifs
Industrial designer attends showings and fairs
Industrial designer studies competing products hands-on
Industrial designer files references in the shared mood board

loop.input: Reference images and photos added to the board.
loop.output: Proposed tags for style, material, colour and product type.
loop.check: The designer confirms or changes each tag; no faces are recognised.
loop.why_not_simpler: Images carry no text to tag by rule.

steps.what: Industrial designer generates design concepts from the references

tasks.design: Saved feeds bring new articles from chosen design publications to one reading list. References from reading, shows and product studies go into a shared mood board where a tagging step proposes style, material and colour tags for the designer to confirm, so earlier references can be found again. Shows, hands-on study and generating concepts stay with the designer.
tasks.previous_blocker: References sat in personal folders without tags.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared boards with proposed image tags.
tasks.still_hard: Turning references into an original concept.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a motif that fits the brand before others do.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; references are easier to find.

reach.learn: Whether shared boards are reused across projects.

evidence.claim: An image archive suggests tags from earlier tags and a person confirms.
Face recognition in an archive processes biometric data and is banned without explicit consent.

assumptions: Boundary: research for inspiration and concepts; detailed design is outside.
Shows, product study and concepts keep their full time.
unknowns: How often old references are reused.

incremental.description: Industrial designer prunes the feed list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly shows and hands-on study, with few articles and references to file (s1 95, s4 80) (3.0); high: heavy desk research and large reference sets (7.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review existing standards and regulations, draft text to develop industrial standards and regulatory guidelines, discuss drafts in committee, process comments, check and submit the comment resolution.

steps.what: Industrial designer reviews existing standards and regulatory guidelines

loop.input: The topic and the company's licensed library of standards and regulations.
loop.output: Relevant clauses with document, clause number and quote.
loop.check: Every quote must match the clause in the library. The designer opens each clause and checks it says what the quote suggests for this topic, including its scope and exceptions, before relying on it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Standards use different terms for the same requirement.

steps.what: Industrial designer drafts the text of industrial standards
Industrial designer discusses drafts in committee meetings
Industrial designer processes comments into the comment resolution table
Industrial designer checks the final comment resolution: each comment has a decision and the decision matches what the committee agreed
Industrial designer submits the approved resolution to the committee secretary

approvals.approved_version: The comment resolution table exactly as checked by the designer in s5, submitted once to the committee secretary; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: A search step over the company's licensed standards library lists relevant clauses with quotes, and the designer opens each one. Comments are collected per clause in a shared table instead of merged from mails. Drafting, committee discussion and the resolution stay with the designer, who checks and submits.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clauses were found by reading whole standards, and comments merged from mails.
tasks.enabler_now: Clause search over licensed libraries and shared comment tables.
tasks.still_hard: Reaching agreement among competitors in a committee.
tasks.human_edge: Writing a requirement that is safe and still allows good design.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; searching and merging shrink.

reach.learn: Whether shared comment tables shorten rounds.

evidence.claim: Research on codes and standards suits an answer desk citing the pages it read.

assumptions: Boundary: the designer's work in a standards committee; publication is the standards body's.
Licensed standards are searched only within the licence terms.
Drafting, discussion, checking and submitting keep their full time; drafting standards text is the designer's own writing.
unknowns: Number of committees the designer sits on.
research_questions: Are relevant clauses missed less often?

already_counted.description: Industrial designer opens and reads listed clauses.

incremental.description: Industrial designer reports outdated documents in the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: narrow standards the designer knows well and few comments (s1 95, s4 85) (2.8); high: broad guidelines touching many standards (8.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review the product line side by side, judge consistency, coordinate the look and function of product lines with engineering, marketing and suppliers, and update the line's design guidelines.

steps.what: Industrial designer reviews the product line side by side: colours, materials, finishes and controls
Industrial designer judges consistency and decides changes to the look and function
Industrial designer aligns changes with engineering, marketing and suppliers
Industrial designer updates the line's design guidelines and finish entries; supplier specification sheets are generated from the changed entries
Industrial designer checks the generated specification sheets before release: colour, material and finish codes and tolerances match the agreed changes
Industrial designer releases the checked specification sheets to the suppliers

tasks.design: Colours, materials, finishes and control layouts for every product in the line sit in one library with renders, so the line can be viewed side by side instead of gathered from files. Specification sheets for suppliers are generated from the library after the designer changes an entry; the designer checks them and releases them once. Judging consistency and agreeing changes stay with the designer.

approvals.approved_version: The specification sheets with colour, material and finish codes exactly as checked by the designer in s4b, released once to the suppliers named on each product; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Finish and colour data were scattered over drawings and supplier sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared colour, material and finish libraries with generated spec sheets.
tasks.still_hard: Older products that cannot be changed.
tasks.human_edge: Making a range feel like one family.

reach.learn: Whether generated spec sheets cut colour mismatches.

evidence.claim: A design tool turns a team's design system into editable layouts.
Spreadsheet trackers are the glue today; a shared library is the record.

assumptions: Boundary: coordinating the line's look and function; designing new products is outside.

Input contract for s1: finish, colour and material entries for each product added once by the designers, with renders from the CAD models; about 80% of the line is in the library; s1 is priced at that share.
Judging and aligning keep their full time. s4 keeps 70: writing the guideline changes stays, but specification sheets are no longer rebuilt by hand.
research_questions: Do finish mismatches across the line fall?

incremental.description: Industrial designer adds new products and finishes to the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about half the line is in the library, so most of the overview and specifications stay by hand (s1 90, s4 85) (3.9); high: about 80% is in the library as assumed (10.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
